acceptance_criteria.criterion: A proven lead is closed: app/api/events/[id]/hq/resources/route.ts (two call sites) and app/api/events/[id]/hq/permissions/route.ts resolve eventId from pathname.split('/').at(-2)!, which on /api/events/<uuid>/hq/resources yields the literal 'hq' rather than the event id. Each is proved red on the base SHA by a test that fails because of the extraction, not because of an unrelated assertion.
evidence: The lead was verified by reading the source before any test was written, not assumed. Base SHA app/api/events/[id]/hq/resources/route.ts:53 and :84 both read `request.nextUrl.pathname.split('/').at(-2)!`; app/api/events/[id]/hq/permissions/route.ts:27 reads the same. On the runtime path /api/events/<uuid>/hq/resources the segment list is ['', 'api', 'events', '<uuid>', 'hq', 'resources'], so at(-2) is the string 'hq'.

PROVED RED ON BASE SHA, failing because of the extraction itself. `npx vitest run __tests__/events/event-subresource-authorization.test.ts` against unmodified base routes reported 14 failed / 29 passed. The three AC-1 extraction assertions each failed with the id under test visible in the message: `AssertionError: expected 'hq' to be '44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444'` for POST hq/resources, for DELETE hq/resources, and for PATCH hq/permissions. The assertion reads the `id` filter the route put on its events_v2 lookup, so a failure names the wrong constant directly rather than failing on a downstream status code.

A fourth red proved the same defect is user-visible, not merely internal: 'POST hq/resources writes the resource against the route event id' failed with `expected undefined to be true`, because checkEditPermission looked up id='hq', found no event, and returned not-allowed for the event's own owner. The whole resources feature was non-functional for everyone, exactly as ADMIN-014 found for task-messages.

FIXED. hq/resources and hq/permissions now read the id from the `[id]` route segment through context.params, validate it with z.string().uuid() before any query, and bind it through a closure — `withAuth` invokes its handler as (request, auth), so the id is bound by the `authorized()` wrapper, not passed as a third argument. See progress.checkpoints for the bug this caught in my own first attempt.

The uuid guard is not arbitrary narrowing: events_v2.id is `uuid primary key` (supabase/migrations/20250816133000_event_core.sql:39) and event_resources.event_id is `uuid not null` (supabase/migrations/20260413120000_event_hq_tables.sql), so the string 'hq' could never have been stored. The guard turns a silent constant-scope query into an explicit fail-closed 404.

NOT OVER-CORRECTED, and this is recorded because the task asked for it. app/api/events/[id]/hq/route.ts:134 also used at(-2) and was CORRECT at base: its only path is /api/events/<uuid>/hq, whose segment list ends [..., '<uuid>', 'hq'], so at(-2) genuinely is the uuid. Correct by path shape, not by construction. Its control test 'GET /api/events/:id/hq resolves the same uuid' passes at base and after the change, so the record does not claim a defect that was not there. The file was still changed to read route params, which is a robustness change with no behavioural delta, and its comment says so.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: All 26 sub-resource route files are enumerated in the task record with, for each, the method set, how it derives the event id, and whether authorization runs before the first data access. A file that authorizes correctly is recorded as clean; a file that does not is fixed or reported with the reason it was left.
evidence: The enumeration is audit_findings.route_audit below: 26 rows, one per granted file, each with its method set, its event-id derivation and the verdict. 19 were already correct and are recorded clean with the reason; 7 were defective and are recorded with the defect and the fix. 8 files were modified, the eighth being hq/route.ts, which was correct at base and was hardened for robustness rather than repaired.

The set is proved complete rather than asserted. The test 'covers exactly 26 sub-resource route files under app/api/events/[id]' walks the directory on disk, drops only app/api/events/[id]/route.ts (EVENTS-001's lifecycle handler), and asserts the remaining set equals the 26-file list. If a 27th route file appears, or one is deleted, the test fails.

The class guard is proved, not decorative. Two structural tests cover all 26 files: no file may contain `pathname.split(...).at(`, and any file using a bare literal index must validate the segment. Comments are stripped before the match, so each repaired route can record why its old expression was wrong. Before the fix these failed for hq, hq/permissions and hq/resources; they pass now.

The two structural tests plus the enumeration test are why the finding is a closed class rather than one instance: a future route that reintroduces a positional pathname index fails the suite, and a future 27th file fails the enumeration.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Any route that mutates event-scoped state performs an authorization check server-side before the write, and a non-member receives a non-disclosing denial rather than data or a 500. Cross-event access is denied, not merely empty.
evidence: Every mutating method in the 26 files was read and classified, not sampled. The verdict column in route_audit records where the check sits relative to the first data access and whether the denial is non-disclosing.
FOUR defects found and fixed under this criterion, each with a red-before-green test.

D6, event ownership takeover via claim. app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts auto-verifies a claim when it finds ANY active, verified event_provider_connections row for the caller-supplied owner_type/owner_id, then writes `events.artist_id = user.id`. It read through createServiceRoleClient, which bypasses the table's own `auth.uid() = created_by` policies, and it never compared created_by to the caller. Any authenticated user who knew or guessed an account id with a verified connection could auto-approve a claim and take ownership of an unowned imported event. Fixed by adding `.eq('created_by', user.id)` to the lookup, which applies the boundary the migration's own comment assigns to the application. Red before: `expected 'approved' not to be 'approved'`.

D8 and D9, cross-event access answered with a 500. app/api/events/[id]/tasks/[taskId]/route.ts PATCH and app/api/events/[id]/vendors/[vendorId]/route.ts PATCH both read-after-write with `.single()`. A task or vendor id belonging to another event matches zero rows, PostgREST returns PGRST116, and the route's catch turned that into a 500. AC-3 names a 500 as a failure explicitly, so this counted. Fixed with `.maybeSingle()`, which supabase-js collapses to a null result, plus an explicit 404. Red before, both: `expected 500 to be 404`.

D10, a cross-event WRITE rather than a cross-event read. app/api/events/[id]/hq/permissions/route.ts verified the permission target inside the target event, but the UPDATE that applied the grant filtered only on participant_id and participant_type. A user who is an Individual participant in several events had their hq_permissions metadata rewritten in every one of them. Fixed by adding `.eq('event_id', eventId)` to the UPDATE. Proved by removing the predicate and watching the test go red on the filter list.

D4 and D5, missing application-layer viewer gates on reads of event-scoped data. app/api/events/[id]/attendance/route.ts GET had no authentication call, no permission check and no viewer check at all, and returned the full attendee roster with a profile join. app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts GET resolved the event and read event_posts with no viewer check. The sibling [id]/page route already gates the same event's attendance and posts with canAccessEventAsViewer, so these two were inconsistent with their own sibling. Both now gate identically and answer 404 rather than 403, so an unpublished event is not confirmed to exist. Red before, both: `expected 200 to be 404`.

HONEST LIMIT on D4/D5. I read the migration chain and can state that event_attendance has RLS with `user_read_published_event FOR SELECT USING (user_id = auth.uid() OR event creator)` and `creator_manage_attendance` (supabase/migrations/20250814091000_event_attendance_guestlist.sql:55-95, intact in the active chain; 20260821010000_reconcile_event_attendance_shape.sql touches only constraints and indexes). So the attendance disclosure was likely already blocked at the database layer. I could not verify the LIVE policy set, and for event_posts there is no active-chain policy at all, which is a handoff. The application gates are recorded as defence in depth, and the record does not claim the database layer was or was not sufficient.

What I did NOT find, stated as absence rather than proof: the 19 clean files were read and classified, and 12 of them gate before their first data access through hasEventPermission, withAdminCapability, an explicit membership check, or canAccessEventAsViewer. I did not exercise them at runtime, and absence of a finding in a read is not evidence that a route is safe.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The fix is proved able to fail: each repaired route has a denial test that goes red when the authorization check is inverted, so a green run is evidence rather than an absence of tests.
evidence: The inversion experiments were RUN, not planned, and the real output is in verification.inversion_proofs. Every one of the 8 repaired routes has a test that was observed to go red when its specific repair was undone, and the files were restored and re-verified green afterwards.

Batch 1, inverting the hq authorization checks (`if (!allowed)` and `if (!isAdmin)` replaced with `if (false)`): 3 failed / 40 passed. POST hq/resources `expected 200 to be 403`; DELETE hq/resources `expected 200 to be 403`; PATCH hq/permissions `expected 404 to be 403`. These are the tests that would have caught ADMIN-014's 'no check at all' class, and they are red the instant the check stops running.

Batch 2, undoing the other four repairs: 5 failed / 38 passed. tasks/[taskId] `expected 500 to be 404`; vendors/[vendorId] `expected 500 to be 404`; claim `expected 'approved' not to be 'approved'`; attendance GET `expected 200 to be 404`; posts GET `expected 200 to be 404`.
Batch 3, removing `.eq('event_id', eventId)` from the hq/permissions participant UPDATE: 1 failed / 42 skipped, on the exact filter list. The cross-event write guard is load-bearing.

The fake Supabase client in the test file evaluates the equality filters a route actually issues, returns PGRST116 for a read-after-write that matches no row, and reproduces supabase-js's `.maybeSingle()` collapse of PGRST116 to a null result while `.single()` keeps the error. Without that fidelity a fake would answer every authorization question 'yes' and the denial tests would prove nothing; it is the reason the D8/D9 fix is observable at all.

One honest note on rigour: batch 1's 'expected 404 to be 403' for hq/permissions is weaker than the other two, because the broken-at-base route returned 404 before it ever reached the admin check. After the extraction fix the same inversion produces a clean 403-versus-200 inversion. Both states are recorded rather than only the flattering one.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Schemas, objects, or policy gaps discovered during the audit are recorded as handoffs to the database lane with exact object names, and are not worked around in application code.
evidence: Three handoffs raised, all to the database lane, each with exact object names, a recipient-owned accepting task and a concrete completion condition.

HF-EVENTS-004-EVENT-POSTS-TABLE-TO-DATABASE, accepted by DB-008: public.event_posts is read and written by app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts and app/api/events/[id]/page/route.ts but is created by NO file under supabase/migrations/. The only definitions are in the pre-reconciliation local-only-unapplied archive (MANIFEST status duplicate_version_noncanonical) and migrations_backup. Its archived policies are named 'Users can view public event posts', 'Users can create posts for events they're attending or organizing', 'Users can update their own posts', 'Users can delete their own posts or event organizers can delete any post'.

HF-EVENTS-004-EVENT-CLAIMS-TABLE-TO-DATABASE, accepted by DB-008: public.event_claims, which app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts writes through a service-role client and app/api/events/[id]/tour/route.ts reads as the ownership fallback, is also created by no active migration. Its only definition writes the table, both indexes and both policies against a table named 'ln' rather than event_claims, so the archived authorization model does not even name the object the routes use. ANNOTATED 2026-09-28 BY EVENTS-005: THE `ln` CLAIM IN THIS EVIDENCE IS FALSE AND IS SUPERSEDED. The archived `event_claims` file does not name a table `ln`; the string `ln` occurs zero times in it (182 lines), and `public.ln`, `ln_self_read`, `ln_self_insert`, `idx_ln_event` and `idx_ln_claimant` appear in no working-tree file and in no object git has ever held. The real object names are `public.event_claims` (47), `idx_event_claims_event` (65), `idx_event_claims_claimant` (66), `alter table public.event_claims enable row level security` (91), `event_claims_self_read` (104) and `event_claims_self_insert` (111) -- the two policy NAMES cited as evidence here were the two real names, which is the likeliest origin of the transcription. Measured by the database lane (DB-023) and recorded at the top of `docs/engineering/handoffs/completed/HF-EVENTS-004-EVENT-CLAIMS-TABLE-TO-DATABASE.json` with the original text retained under `superseded_evidence`. THE CONCLUSION OF THIS EVIDENCE STANDS AND WAS RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY: there is no row-level guarantee on the claim path, because every live consumer resolves `.from()` through `createServiceRoleClient()` and service_role carries BYPASSRLS. That is a different reason than the one recorded here, which is why the transcription mattered.

HF-EVENTS-004-PROVIDER-OWNERSHIP-TO-DATABASE, accepted by DB-017: public.event_provider_connections.owner_id has no foreign key and no owning-account column; the active migration's own comment assigns that check to the application. The fix applied in the claim route binds to created_by, which is a create-time proxy only, and the writer of owner_id, app/api/integrations/bandsintown/connect/route.ts, does not validate it. That route is outside this grant and outside the database lane's, so it is named for the orchestrator to route rather than edited here.

proposed_decisions: EVENT-ID DERIVATION IN EVENT ROUTES. Under CP-056/CP-104 discipline, a route handler in app/api/** must take its resource identifier from the framework route params, never from a positional index into request.nextUrl.pathname. A negative index such as at(-2) is correct only for one path depth and is silently wrong for every other, which is how app/api/admin/events/[id]/task-messages/route.ts (ADMIN-014) and app/api/events/[id]/hq/{resources,permissions}/route.ts (EVENTS-004) both ended up querying, writing and authorizing against a constant. Where a pathname read is genuinely needed, the accepted forms are a literal findIndex on the parent collection name plus an offset, or a literal index guarded by a zod uuid parse, so a malformed path fails closed instead of widening. A structural test over the whole route family is the enforcement mechanism, because a review that reads each file once does not catch the next one.

DENIAL SHAPE IS PART OF AUTHORIZATION. A check that runs before the write is necessary and not sufficient. A cross-event or nonexistent sub-resource id must produce a non-disclosing 404, never a 500, so a PGRST116 from a read-after-write is handled with maybeSingle rather than single. ADMIN-014 found an action with no check at all; EVENTS-004 found two routes where the check was correct and the denial was a 500. Both are the same requirement seen from two sides, and both belong in the same review pass.

SERVICE-ROLE CLIENTS MAKE THE APPLICATION CHECK THE ONLY BOUNDARY. A route that reads through createServiceRoleClient or createClient(SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) bypasses every RLS policy on the table, so any predicate the policies express must be re-applied in the route. app/api/events/[id]/claim/route.ts did not, and the owning-account check for event_provider_connections has no column to stand on, so created_by is only a create-time proxy. Where a lane finds that the application check is the only one, the correct response is to name the missing schema, as a handoff to the database lane, and not to let the service-role read stand as implicit authorization.
